title: Stargazing in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Two public observatories open their telescopes at night this autumn:** the Archenhold Observatory in Treptower Park and the Wilhelm-Foerster Observatory on the Insulaner in Schöneberg.
**Nacht auf der Sternwarte costs €12, or €8 reduced,** runs 90 minutes, is for ages 12 and up, and starts at 20:00 or 22:00.
**Archenhold opens Thursday to Saturday** with its 500 mm mirror telescope and 42 seats; **Wilhelm-Foerster opens Friday and Saturday** with its 12-inch Bamberg refractor and 50 seats.
**Saturn is at opposition on 4 October.** In October the 22:00 session sees it higher; after the clocks go back on 25 October, 20:00 is fully dark.
**The darkest weekends** are 9 and 10 October, 6 and 7 November, 13 and 14 November, 4 and 5 December and 11 and 12 December.
**Telescope sessions are in German.** The English options are the Starry Night and Encounters in the Milky Way dome shows.
**One simple move: pick a Friday or Saturday with the Moon down and Saturn up,** then book that session before the 20:00 seats go.
